questions.q: What does differential privacy mathematically guarantee?
options: That a model will never produce an incorrect prediction
That a model's training data is fully encrypted at rest
That no attacker can ever query the model's API more than once
That the presence or absence of any single record in a dataset can only change a computation's output by a precisely bounded amount
questions.explain: Differential privacy is a mathematical guarantee, not an operational control — it bounds, in a way you can quantify in advance, how much including or excluding any one record can change the output of a computation on the dataset.

questions.q: What does the privacy budget, epsilon, control?
options: The strength of the privacy guarantee — smaller epsilon means more noise and a stronger guarantee, at a cost to accuracy
The number of servers the model is deployed across
The number of employees allowed to access the training data
The exact dollar cost of running the model in production
questions.explain: Epsilon is a tradeoff dial: smaller epsilon adds more calibrated noise and produces a stronger privacy guarantee, while larger epsilon adds less noise but weakens the guarantee — accuracy and privacy trade directly against each other.

questions.q: What does DP-SGD, introduced by Abadi et al. (2016), actually do during training?
options: It clips each training example's gradient contribution to a bounded norm and adds calibrated noise to the aggregated gradient before updating model weights
It encrypts the final trained model weights file
It removes all sensitive records from the training set entirely before training begins
It only applies after training is complete, during inference
questions.explain: DP-SGD modifies the standard training loop itself: clipping per-example gradients so no single record dominates a step, then adding noise to the aggregated gradient, producing a provable DP guarantee baked into the model's parameters.

questions.q: Why does bounding a single record's influence on a model directly defend against membership inference?
options: It doesn't — differential privacy has no relationship to membership inference
If removing any one record can't meaningfully change the model's output, there's no reliable confidence-gap signal left for a shadow model to detect that record's presence
It works only by physically deleting the record from the database after training
It works by making the model refuse to answer any query at all
questions.explain: Membership inference exploits the confidence gap between memorized and unseen data. If no single record is allowed to meaningfully shift the model's behavior, that gap shrinks toward nothing, removing the signal shadow models rely on.

questions.q: Which of these is a real, production deployment of differential privacy described in this lesson?
options: The U.S. Census Bureau adopted differential privacy for the 2020 Census to publish useful statistics while protecting individual households
Differential privacy has only ever been tested in academic papers and has never been deployed at scale
Differential privacy is exclusively used for encrypting network traffic
Differential privacy requires removing all noise from query results to work correctly
questions.explain: The U.S. Census Bureau adopted differential privacy for the 2020 Census specifically to protect individual household data while publishing useful population statistics; Apple and Google have similarly used it for telemetry.
